functions.name: yaml_scalar
functions.behavior: Decode the minimal set of YAML scalar quoting forms Copilot emits in workspace.yaml. Trim leading/trailing whitespace first. Empty, `null`, or `~` -> empty string. Double-quoted (`"..."`, starts AND ends with `"`): try to JSON-parse the whole token; if it parses to a JSON string, return that string; if it parses to a non-string JSON value, return empty; if JSON parsing fails, fall back to stripping only the first and last byte (value[1:-1]). Single-quoted (`'...'`): strip first/last char and replace every `''` with a single `'`. Anything else: return the (already-trimmed) value verbatim.
edge_cases: Input is only whitespace -> trimmed to "" -> returns "".
Literal tokens `null` and `~` (already trimmed) -> ""; but `null` with other text e.g. `nullish` is returned verbatim.
A lone `"` (len 1) satisfies both startswith and endswith on the same char in Python; json.loads("\"") fails -> value[1:-1] == "" . Rust must guard len<2 so the strip yields "" not a panic/underflow.
`""` (empty double-quoted) -> json.loads -> "" -> returns "".

Double-quoted token that is valid JSON but not a string, e.g. `"123"` is still a JSON string so returns `123`; a token like `"true"` returns `true` (it IS a quoted string). Only bare-looking quoted tokens that JSON-decode to non-string (not reachable when both ends are literal quote chars) return "" — preserve the isinstance(str) guard anyway for exact parity.
Malformed double-quoted (embedded unescaped quote) -> JSON error -> returns inner bytes via value[1:-1] (NOT re-unescaped).
Single-quoted with doubled quotes `'it''s'` -> `it's`.
No quotes and not a null token -> returned as-is after trim (e.g. plain `myproject`).

functions.name: workspace_field
functions.behavior: Read one TOP-LEVEL (column-0, unindented) scalar or block-scalar field named `key` from a workspace.yaml text. Split text into lines (Python str.splitlines semantics). For the FIRST line that starts with `key + ":"`: take the remainder after the prefix, trimmed. If that remainder is a block-scalar indicator (`|`, `|-`, `|+`, `>`, `>-`, `>+`), scan subsequent lines: stop at the first continuation line whose first char is non-whitespace (i.e. a new top-level key), and return the first non-empty continuation line, trimmed; if none, return "". Otherwise return yaml_scalar(remainder). If no line matches the prefix, return "".
edge_cases: Only the FIRST occurrence of `key:` is honored (early return), not the last.
Key must be at column 0: an indented `  name:` under some parent is ignored — startswith(prefix) is a raw string-prefix test, no YAML nesting awareness.

Prefix is `key + ":"` with no space, so `name:foo` (no space after colon) still matches and yields `foo` after trim; `names: x` does NOT match `name:` because after the prefix the next char is `s`... actually it does NOT match because startswith("name:") is false for "names:" — verify: "names:".startswith("name:") is False (position 4 is 's' not ':'). Preserve.
Block scalar returns ONLY the first non-empty continuation line, stripped — it does NOT join/fold the whole literal or folded block. Deliberate quirk.
A block whose continuation lines are all blank/whitespace -> returns "".

Block termination: a continuation line whose first character is non-whitespace ends the block even if blank-check would have skipped it; an EMPTY continuation line (len 0) does NOT terminate (it fails the `continuation and not continuation[0].isspace()` guard because empty is falsy) and is simply skipped.

PARITY: Python str.splitlines() splits on many boundaries (
, , 
, \v,  , \x1c-\x1e, \x85,  ,  ) and drops a trailing empty line; Rust str::lines() only splits on 
 and 
. Use a splitlines-equivalent if exotic separators are possible, though real workspace.yaml uses 
.
isspace on first char uses Python's unicode whitespace definition; Rust char::is_whitespace differs slightly (e.g. Python treats some chars differently). Real indentation is space/tab so low risk.

functions.name: copilot_title
functions.behavior: Return the current Copilot session display name: workspace_field(text, "name") or, if empty, workspace_field(text, "summary"), reduced to its first non-empty trimmed line. Path is ~/.copilot/session-state/<session_id>/workspace.yaml. Uses a per-workspace-path cache keyed on st_mtime_ns: on an mtime hit, return the cached title without re-reading. On a miss, read+parse, and if the freshly computed title is empty but a cached value exists, keep the cached (previous) title. Store (mtime_ns, title) back into the cache.
functions.side_effects: Filesystem: os.stat + open/read of workspace.yaml. Mutates the copilot title cache (LabelCache.copilot). Reads ~ (home dir) expansion.
edge_cases: Empty session_id -> "" immediately (no stat).
stat fails (file missing) -> "" and cache untouched.
stat succeeds but open/read fails (transient race) -> "" returned WITHOUT writing cache and WITHOUT falling back to the previous cached value (differs from the empty-title-keeps-cache path).
mtime hit returns cached title verbatim (even if empty).
Fresh scan empty + cache present -> keeps previous title (sticky).
Fresh scan empty + no cache -> stores (mtime_ns, "").
title is reduced via first-non-empty-line-strip AFTER the name/summary or-fallback, so a multiline `name` value collapses to its first non-blank line.
Cache key MUST be st_mtime_ns (integer nanoseconds), matching Python exactly, so invalidation cadence is identical; do NOT reuse the Claude float-seconds mtime here.
Home-dir expansion: os.path.expanduser(~) — replicate with the same HOME resolution.

functions.name: scan_tail
functions.signature: fn scan_tail(transcript_path: &Path) -> (String, String, String, String, String)
functions.behavior: Read the final _TITLE_TAIL_BYTES (65536) bytes of a Claude transcript and extract (custom, ai, agent, team, color). Seek to max(0, size-65536), read to EOF, split on b'\n'. If size > 65536, drop the first (likely truncated) line. Iterate all lines; for each, a byte-substring prefilter selects at most ONE branch (elif chain): `"custom-title"` -> parse, if type==custom-title and truthy customTitle set custom; else-if `"ai-title"` -> if type==ai-title and truthy aiTitle set ai; else-if `"agent-color"` -> if type==agent-color and truthy agentColor set color; else-if (agent or team still unset) and `"agentName"` present -> parse, if type != agent-name set agent = agent-or-agentName-or-empty and team = team-or-teamName-or-empty. custom/ai/color are LAST-wins (overwritten each match); agent/team are FIRST-wins (only filled while empty). JSON parse failure (incl. invalid utf-8) on any line -> skip that line.
functions.side_effects: Filesystem: open (binary), seek, read of the transcript tail. No cache mutation (pure w.r.t. state; only reads the file).
edge_cases: OSError opening/seeking/reading -> returns ("","","","","").
Truncated-first-line drop happens ONLY when size > 65536; for a small file the first line is kept.

Byte-substring prefilter runs BEFORE JSON parse (perf), and the branches are mutually exclusive per line (elif): a line containing `"custom-title"` is never also inspected for agentName even if it contains that substring too.

custom/ai/color: last matching record in the tail wins (forward iteration, unconditional assign). agent/team: FIRST non-empty in the tail wins (guarded by `not agent`/`not team` and `x or y` fallback). This asymmetry MUST be preserved.
Truthiness gates: empty-string customTitle/aiTitle/agentColor do NOT set the field (falsy). agentName/teamName use `or ""` so None/empty -> "".

Teammate detection: agentName/teamName are read only from records whose type != 'agent-name' (a teammate stamps them on every conversation record; a normal session only carries agentName inside a rename 'agent-name' record which is deliberately excluded).

Wrong-type but substring-present line (e.g. `"custom-title"` appearing as a value while type is something else): the branch runs, condition fails, nothing set, and no other branch is tried for that line.
Invalid UTF-8 in a line: Python json.loads(bytes) raises UnicodeDecodeError (subclass of ValueError) -> caught -> skip. Rust: treat decode failure as skip.

split on b'\n' (not splitlines): a trailing \r from CRLF stays attached to the line but doesn't affect substring/JSON parsing; and a trailing empty final element from a terminating newline is harmless.
Very large transcript: only the 64KiB tail is ever read; correctness relies on Claude rewriting title records near EOF each turn.

functions.name: claude_session_meta
functions.behavior: Resolve (title, agent_name, team, color) for a Claude session, with sticky caching keyed on transcript_path and invalidated by float getmtime. On an mtime hit, return cached (title, agent, team, color) — note the internal is_custom flag (cache index 2) is retained across ticks but not returned. On a miss, scan_tail then resolve title: custom -> (custom, is_custom=true); elif prev_custom -> (prev_title, true) [sticky manual rename survives later ai-titles]; elif ai -> (ai, false); else -> (prev_title, prev_custom) [keep last]. agent/team/color each fall back to their previous cached value when the fresh scan is empty (sticky). Store the 6-tuple (mtime, title, is_custom, agent, team, color).
functions.side_effects: Filesystem: getmtime + (via scan_tail) reads the transcript tail. Mutates the Claude title cache (LabelCache.title). The `_session_id` parameter is accepted for dispatch symmetry but ignored.
edge_cases: Empty transcript_path (legacy 2-field registry record or just-started session) -> ("","","","") with NO stat/read.
getmtime OSError (file vanished) -> ("","","","") and cache untouched.
mtime hit short-circuits: returns cached title/agent/team/color without re-scanning.

Sticky is_custom: a manual /rename ('custom-title') stays the shown title even as Claude keeps emitting 'ai-title' records, because prev_custom forces the elif branch. This is the single most important stateful invariant.
Sticky agent/team/color: a burst of output can push these out of the 64KiB tail; the prev_* fallbacks keep the last-seen value. Must NOT regress to "".
Return drops is_custom (only title/agent/team/color surface); is_custom lives solely in the cache to drive stickiness.

PARITY: cache invalidation key is float os.path.getmtime (seconds), compared with exact equality — distinct from copilot's mtime_ns. Store the same representation and compare exactly to match re-scan cadence.
First-ever miss with no cache: prev_title="", prev_custom=false, prev_agent/team/color=""; if scan finds nothing everything stays "".
Float mtime equality: two writes within the same filesystem timestamp granularity look identical and skip the re-scan — replicate by using the same timestamp source/precision the platform gives.

functions.name: copilot_session_meta
functions.behavior: Return SessionMeta { title: copilot_title(cache, session_id), agent_name: "", team: "", color: "" }. Copilot exposes no teammate identity or color metadata in this codepath. The transcript_path parameter is accepted for dispatch symmetry and ignored.
functions.side_effects: Delegates to copilot_title (filesystem read of workspace.yaml + copilot cache mutation).
edge_cases: agent_name/team/color are ALWAYS empty for Copilot, which downstream means no team-color fallback and label composed as a top-level (non-teammate) session.
Ignores transcript_path entirely (Copilot title comes from workspace.yaml, not the transcript).

functions.name: session_meta
functions.signature: fn session_meta(cache: &mut LabelCache, transcript_path: &str, agent: &str, session_id: &str) -> SessionMeta
functions.behavior: Dispatch to the per-agent handler by exact `agent` string: "claude" -> claude_session_meta(transcript_path, session_id); "copilot" -> copilot_session_meta(transcript_path, session_id). Any other/unknown/empty agent -> SessionMeta::empty (all four fields ""). This is the sole public metadata entry point; callers in assoc (title matching) and rows (label building) use it.
functions.side_effects: Whatever the dispatched handler does (filesystem + cache). No side effect for unknown agents.
edge_cases: Unknown/empty agent -> all-empty result, treated as a no-metadata session (never an error).
Dispatch is by exact case-sensitive match against the handler map keys 'claude'/'copilot'.
session_id is passed to both handlers; claude ignores it, copilot uses it as the workspace directory name.
Default caller derives session_id by stripping the `<agent>-` prefix from the registry id when present, else the whole id (sidebar.py:449-450) — the labels module receives the already-stripped id.

functions.name: label_mode_from
functions.behavior: Normalize a raw @wrangler-label option string to a mode enum: LabelMode::Dir if value.trim().to_lowercase() == "dir", else LabelMode::Name (the default for unset/unknown/whitespace/empty).
functions.side_effects: none (pure). Note the caller supplies the raw value from `tmux show-option -gqv @wrangler-label`; the tmux read is NOT in this function.
edge_cases: Only the exact trimmed+lowercased token "dir" selects Dir; everything else (including "directory", "", unset, mixed junk) -> Name.
Case-insensitive and whitespace-insensitive via strip().lower().
Empty/unset tmux option (show-option -gqv returns empty) -> Name.

functions.name: agent_label
functions.signature: fn agent_label(mode: LabelMode, title: &str, agent_name: &str, dir_name: &str) -> String
functions.behavior: Compose the exact agent-row label text. If agent_name is non-empty (a teammate): tail = title (Name mode) or dir_name (Dir mode); return `@{agent_name} - {tail}` when tail is non-empty, else `@{agent_name}`. If agent_name is empty (top-level session): return (title if Name mode else "") falling back to dir_name when that is empty — i.e. Name mode shows title or dir_name-if-untitled; Dir mode always shows dir_name.
edge_cases: Separator is ` - ` (space, ASCII hyphen-minus, space) — NOT an em dash; preserve the exact three characters.
Untitled teammate in Name mode: tail=title="" -> `@{name}` with no trailing separator (the dir fallback is deliberately dropped so an un-named-turn teammate stays `@name`).
Untitled teammate in Dir mode: tail=dir_name (could itself be "" -> `@{name}`).
Top-level Name mode untitled: ("" ) or dir_name -> dir_name.
Top-level Dir mode: ("") or dir_name -> dir_name (title never shown).

dir_name is computed by the caller as os.path.basename(display_cwd.rstrip('/')) or display_cwd (sidebar.py:502) — an empty/edge cwd falls back to the full path; the labels module receives the finished dir_name string and must not re-derive it.
All-empty inputs (no agent_name, no title, empty dir_name) -> "".

parity_risks: STICKY CACHED STATE (highest risk): both caches are module-global mutable dicts in Python. _title_cache retains an is_custom flag that is never returned but makes a manual /rename title override every subsequent ai-title. _copilot_title_cache keeps the last title when a fresh read is empty. In Rust these become owned state (e.g. a LabelCache struct held by the sidebar loop, or a Mutex/RefCell if shared); the module is NOT pure. Losing either stickiness path (title, is_custom, agent, team, color for Claude; title for Copilot) changes what the sidebar shows during output bursts.

MTIME KEY MISMATCH BY DESIGN: Claude uses float os.path.getmtime (seconds), Copilot uses st_mtime_ns (int). They must stay distinct and be compared with exact equality; using a single unified timestamp type risks changing re-scan cadence. Float-equality on mtime means sub-granularity rewrites skip re-scan — replicate exactly.

SCAN-TAIL ORDERING ASYMMETRY: custom-title/ai-title/agent-color are LAST-wins (unconditional overwrite while iterating forward); agentName/teamName are FIRST-wins (guarded by `not agent`/`not team`). Forward iteration order over the tail lines is load-bearing.

BYTE-SUBSTRING PREFILTER + ELIF EXCLUSIVITY in scan_tail: each line is classified into at most one branch by the first matching byte substring, BEFORE JSON parse. A line is never checked against a later branch's substring. Reordering the checks or parsing every line unconditionally can change results on adversarial/multi-field lines.
TRUNCATED-FIRST-LINE DROP: lines[0] is deleted only when size > 65536. Off-by-one here either drops a real record on small files or keeps a corrupt partial record on large ones.

BOUNDED TAIL READ: only the final 65536 bytes are scanned; correctness depends on Claude keeping title records near EOF. The sticky cache is what covers the transient case where they scroll out — the two mechanisms are coupled.

TRUTHINESS/EMPTY GATES: empty-string customTitle/aiTitle/agentColor must NOT set their field; agentName/teamName use `or ""`. And downstream 'EMPTY TITLE NEVER MATCHES' (assoc, sidebar.py:465-467): a session whose title is "" is unassociable by title. Returning "" vs a stray space changes association behavior.

SPLITLINES SEMANTICS: _workspace_field and _copilot_title use Python str.splitlines() (many unicode line boundaries, drops trailing empty); _scan_tail uses split(b'
'). Rust str::lines()/split('
') differ on exotic separators and trailing-empty handling. Real files use 
 so low but non-zero risk.

YAML SCALAR DECODE QUIRKS: double-quoted path falls back to naive first/last-byte strip on JSON error (not proper unescaping); single-quoted does only `''`->`'`; block scalars return only the FIRST non-empty continuation line (no fold/join). len<2 quoted tokens must not underflow in Rust.

MUTUAL-EXCLUSION INVARIANT (upstream, affects meaning of markers not labels, but relevant to the row's status the caller pairs with the label): attention vs working markers are mutually exclusive (hook + sidebar.py:492-494); labels itself does not touch markers but its output is rendered alongside them.

CROSS-MODULE COUPLING / CONSUMERS: labels is a LEAF (imports only json+os, no code-level project deps). Its declared depends_on are DATA-CONTRACT deps: `hook` owns the registry record format (transcript path, agent field, id) from which transcript_path/agent/session_id are derived (rows/assoc pass them in), and `tmux` supplies the raw @wrangler-label string to label_mode_from. Reverse consumers: `rows` (agent_label + label_mode_from), `assoc` (session_meta title for pane association), `color` (team_pane_colors fallback is gated on the color/agent_name fields session_meta returns; team_pane_colors itself lives in the color/rows concern, NOT in labels). Do not accidentally pull team_pane_colors into the labels port.

LEGACY RECORD BACK-COMPAT: a legacy 2-field registry record yields an empty transcript_path; claude_session_meta must short-circuit to all-empty (title/agent/team/color) rather than stat an empty path.
SEPARATOR CHARACTER: agent_label uses ` - ` (ASCII hyphen), never an em dash — matches the user's project rule; keep it byte-exact.
UNKNOWN-AGENT DISPATCH: session_meta returns all-empty (not an error/panic) for any agent string outside {claude, copilot}; the enum/dispatch in Rust must have that catch-all.
